coverage: Curated, non-exhaustive sourced litigation and administration developments; reported record volumes are not disenfranchised voter counts

methodology.primary_metric: Potentially affected voters or ballots, only when grounded in a cited primary source
count_rules: Never equate records flagged, lawsuits filed, or challenges submitted with votes lost.
Record separate counts for potentially exposed, confirmed affected, remedied, and unresolved; unknown values are null.
Never subtract remediations from exposure without proof they refer to the same population.
Never sum potentially overlapping incidents into a statewide unique-voter total.
Preserve units: voters, ballots, registrations, and records are not interchangeable.
Store earliest/latest date, geographic scope, mechanism, source and verification status for each incident.
Do not infer partisan effects or probability of fraud from incident counts.

monitoring_priority_v1.definition: 0–100 provisional operational monitoring score, NOT a probability of fraud or a calibrated probability of affected voters.
scoring_rules: Documented voter-list disclosure litigation without shown voting-access consequences: 4 points.
Documented change to early-voting opportunity: 18 points; +2 when the change covers at least 10 counties.
Documented voter-registration transmission/processing incident: 25 points; -4 if the transfer defect is officially reported fixed but processing outcomes remain unverified.
Never use raw registration-record counts as counts of unique voters at risk.
Unverified reports cannot increase the index. Fully resolved cases require manual review rather than automatic treatment as active.
A state's provisional score is the maximum distinct documented incident score, not the sum of litigation, press articles or overlapping incidents.
Actual confirmed disenfranchisement would trigger a re-review and replacement of this starter rubric, not an arbitrary automatic extra point.
monitoring_priority_v1.missingness: Absence of an incident in the curated tracker is Not assessed, not 0. Unknown probabilities and voter counts remain null.
monitoring_priority_v1.roadmap: Move to severity × bounded unique voter exposure × probability of the precisely defined adverse outcome, once incident-level estimates are supported and can be reviewed.

probability_model_v0.headline: Subjective scenario probability, not a measured statistical frequency or fraud probability.
probability_model_v0.common_event: At least 100 distinct otherwise-eligible voters cannot cast a countable ballot solely because of the specified incident, by the conclusion of ordinary ballot review.
probability_model_v0.method: Transparent judgmental starting priors by observed mechanism, discounted for documented remedies and alternative voting opportunities. Rounded point assessments with wide explicit ranges. No observed frequencies or empirical calibration claimed.
priors: Direct registration processing backlog with remediation opportunities: 12% central, 3–30% subjective range.
Reduction in voting-time options with alternative voting opportunities: 10% central, 2–25% subjective range.
Litigation with no implemented voting-access change: 1% central, 0.1–5% subjective range.
caveats: The ranges are analysts' working assumptions, not probability distributions calibrated from historical outcomes.
Numbers refer to an adverse operational access outcome affecting at least 100 people, not to fraud, vote suppression intent, or an altered election result.
A documented decrease in voting convenience may be certain even if 100 people failing to vote is unlikely.
No automatic partisan adjustments; source conditions, remedies and actual ballot outcomes drive updates.
An incident's reported records, counties or historical Sunday turnout may contextualize exposure but are not counts of disenfranchised voters.

incidents.title: Maine — DOJ voter-list disclosure litigation
incidents.summary: Dismissed at district court; appeal ongoing. Litigation concerns access to statewide voter-list data; no count of eligible voters denied voting is established by this source.

adverse_scenario.definition: At least 100 otherwise-eligible voters become unable to cast countable ballots by the conclusion of normal review as a direct consequence of voter-list changes resulting from this litigation. Filing or pursuing a lawsuit alone does not satisfy the scenario.
adverse_scenario.worst_case_source: Not established; requires voter-level deduplication, affected voters and counterfactual access data.
adverse_scenario.probability_basis: 1% subjective reference scenario probability (0.1–5% uncertainty range). These voter-list disclosure lawsuits have no documented ballot-access change. A new operational order, implemented voter removal, or proof of adverse access impact would require immediate reassessment. Not calibrated from historical cases.

exposure_proxy.notes: Statewide voter list access is not itself a population of disenfranchised voters.

incidents.title: Texas registration-record transmission backlog
incidents.summary: Texas DPS says the data-transfer defect was corrected September 13. At least 500,000 delayed registration/update records were subsequently delivered to counties; statewide processing completion and voter-level consequences are not established.
incidents.count_source_notes: Reported statewide backlog of at least 500,000 registration and update records; does not establish unique individuals or ballots.

sources.publisher: Texas Secretary of State Elections Division (Sept. 22 directive)
Texas Secretary of State — county processing help, Sept. 25
Votebeat / Texas Tribune — provisional ballot remedy, Sept. 22
Texas Tribune — system glitches slowing processing, Oct. 5

incidents.process_status: Transfer defect fixed per Texas DPS; county processing completion not established statewide
incidents.scope_note: Records, not unique voters or lost votes

adverse_scenario.definition: At least 100 distinct otherwise-eligible Texans fail to cast countable ballots by conclusion of ordinary review because their timely DPS-related registrations or updates remained unprocessed despite available remedies.
adverse_scenario.worst_case_source: Not established; requires voter-level deduplication, affected voters and counterfactual access data.
adverse_scenario.probability_basis: 12% subjective central estimate (3–30% range) for >=100 distinct eligible voters unable to cast countable ballots because of this transfer backlog. Upward factors: 500,000+ delayed registration/update records, county processing difficulties ahead of the registration deadline. Downward factors: transfer defect reportedly fixed, state assistance to counties, and provisional-ballot remedies for timely applications. No count of unique affected people or calibrated failure rate exists.

exposure_proxy.notes: Documented backlog volume, NOT unique voters, not the upper bound on all delayed transactions, and not ballots lost.

incidents.title: Sunday early-voting hours removed in 10 counties
incidents.summary: The state elections board approved early-voting plans eliminating Sunday hours in ten counties that offered them in 2022. This is a change in access options; the number of voters whose ballots are affected is unknown.
incidents.process_status: Early-voting schedule approved; Sunday hours removed in 10 counties relative to 2022
incidents.scope_note: No count of voters unable to cast a ballot established

adverse_scenario.definition: At least 100 otherwise-eligible North Carolina voters who would use the discontinued Sunday early-voting hours in the named 10 counties do not cast a countable ballot by the conclusion of ordinary review, despite other voting opportunities.
adverse_scenario.worst_case_source: Not established; requires voter-level deduplication, affected voters and counterfactual access data.
adverse_scenario.probability_basis: 10% subjective central estimate (2–25% range) for >=100 otherwise-eligible voters unable to cast countable ballots as a direct consequence of the removed Sunday hours. Downward factor: other early-voting days, election-day and mail options remain. Upward uncertainty: access constraints for Sunday-dependent voters; historical county Sunday turnout and alternate-hours capacity are not yet quantified. No calibrated turnout counterfactual.

exposure_proxy.notes: Geographic scope, NOT number of people prevented from voting. 2022 county Sunday voting figures still require retrieval.

incidents.title: North Carolina — 1,392 planned SAVE citizenship-check letters
incidents.mechanism: Official election-administration notice to voters flagged for additional citizenship verification
incidents.summary: On October 13 the State Board of Elections announced plans to send letters during the week to 1,392 registered voters flagged by federal SAVE data, after additional agency reviews. The board explicitly says a letter does not cancel registration or automatically bar voting, and no one is removed solely on SAVE information. Source does not establish that the mailings have been delivered, anyone is ineligible, or any eligible voter has lost a countable ballot.

sources.publisher: North Carolina State Board of Elections — Oct. 13, 2026 press release

incidents.scope_label: 1,392 registrants slated for SAVE follow-up letters
incidents.scope_note: Number of registered voter records selected for planned correspondence, from the Board's Oct. 13 announcement, not confirmed mailed letters or unique eligible voters denied voting.
incidents.process_status: Board announced notification and review; no automatic removal from notice alone

adverse_scenario.definition: At least 100 otherwise-eligible NC registrants become unable to cast countable November 2026 ballots solely because of this citizenship-notice process after ordinary review and remedies; receiving a letter alone does not meet the definition.
adverse_scenario.worst_case_source: Not quantified: requires verified removal/challenge outcomes, eligible-person identity, correction and provisional ballot disposition.
adverse_scenario.probability_basis: Insufficient evidence to estimate a probability of countable ballots lost; the official source explicitly rules out automatic removal or cancellation based solely on the notice.

exposure_proxy.unit: registered voters selected for planned letters
exposure_proxy.qualifier: announced notification scope, NOT ballots lost
exposure_proxy.notes: Official Oct. 13 statement after additional state checks; no verified removal or ballot-prevention count. Do not conflate recipients with affected eligible voters.
